texts: Domain Knowledge, Business Logic & Stakeholder Guide
Global Partner Solutions  |  MCAPS Data Engineering  |  FY26
This deck explains the business meaning behind CoSell — what the domain represents,how key decisions are encoded in data, and the logic that drives every metric.
The business purpose and who it serves
A glossary of CoSell-specific terms every stakeholder should know
From referral creation to revenue recognition — the end-to-end journey
How Microsoft and Partners initiate co-sell deals differently
The Oct-2018 cutoff rule and dual/triple fallback exchange rate strategy
How deals get flagged: Closed, Accepted, ISV, YTD-eligible, Won
Measuring speed-to-approval, speed-to-close, and inbound response time
The chain: MPN ID → PartnerMaster → PartnerOne → Sub → ReportingKey
The 3rd-of-month boundary rule that determines fiscal credit
How customer and partner geography cascade from account data
Business rules for IP partner deals, bundled ACR, and marketplace ACV
Investment bridge analytics and funnel categorization
What transforms at each Medallion layer and why
The reporting scenarios this data powers
The business problem it solves and who depends on it

The Business Problem
Microsoft partners (ISVs, SIs, resellers) co-sell Microsoft products alongside their own solutions. Tracking whether a partner referral turned into a real opportunity, whether revenue was recognized, and how fast deals progressed through the funnel requires combining data from multiple disconnected systems (Partner Center, MSX/CRM, currency tables, account hierarchies).

What CoSell Does
CoSell unifies this data into a single analytical model that answers:
  •  Did a partner referral convert into a Microsoft sales opportunity?
  •  How fast did Microsoft respond (inbound velocity)?
  •  What is the deal worth in USD across 9 different financial measures?
  •  Was the partner's CRM account co-sell-ready (ISV eligible)?
  •  Which scorecard month gets fiscal credit for this deal?
  •  What is the partner's quantitative impact on Microsoft's business (PIN)?

Who Depends on CoSell
GPS Leadership, Partner Development Managers, Finance (revenue attribution), Field Sellers (scorecard credit), ISV Program (co-sell readiness tracking), CoMarketing (investment ROI).
80+ Gold TablesDimensional model covering the full deal lifecycle
9 USD Financial MetricsWith sophisticated multi-currency exchange rate logic
12 Performance MetricsVelocity, acceptance, ISV engagement, win rates
5 Source Systems UnifiedPartner Center, MSX/CRM, Hub, Currency, Revenue Account
PIN MetricsPartner Impact Numbers across E5 Security, CSP Copilot, etc.
The language of CoSell — terms every stakeholder must know
A joint selling motion where Microsoft and a partner collaborate to sell to a customer. The partner refers a deal (or Microsoft refers to the partner), and both work together through the sales cycle.
A deal initiated in Partner Center by a partner (Outbound from MS perspective) or sent to a partner by Microsoft (Inbound). Each gets a unique PSXDealID. This is the atomic unit of CoSell tracking.

Microsoft's unified partner identity. A single partner may have multiple MPN IDs, but PartnerOne consolidates them into one hierarchy: PartnerOneID → PartnerOneSubKey (subsidiary level) → PartnerOneReportingKey (rolled-up for reporting).

The lifecycle stage of a deal: Support 100%, Deploy 100%, MS Win 100% (positive closures), or Disengaged 0%, Loss 0% (negative closures). A deal is 'Closed' when it reaches any of these terminal stages.
A flag on the partner's CRM account (IsCoSellReadyPartnerAccount). Only deals from ISV co-sell-ready partners are counted in ISVDealsReporting. This is an eligibility gate, not a deal attribute.
A flag (IsDealWithPartnerGTM) indicating the deal participates in Microsoft's Partner GTM program. Used as a prerequisite for IsDealAccepted and IsOpportunityWon calculations.

A quantitative measure of partner contribution to Microsoft's business. Metrics like E5 Security Usage and CSP Copilot Seats are per-partner (Non-Aggregate); others can be summed across partners (Aggregate).
The actual Azure consumption revenue attributed to partner deals. PartnerReportedACR is self-reported by partners; TrueACRConsumption is system-verified.
The fiscal month a deal gets credited to. Governed by the 3rd-of-month rule: deals approved after the 3rd → current month; before the 3rd → prior month.
Microsoft's internal sales org structure. Mapped via MSSalesID → ATUID from DimRevenueAccount. Connects deals to the field sales team responsible.
End-to-end journey from referral to revenue — and the data captured at each stage
Partner creates a deal inPartner Center (or MSFTrefers to partner).Data: PSXDealID, Direction(Inbound/Outbound),CreatedDate, MPNId
MSFT or Partner accepts.Deal linked to MSXOpportunity.Data: AcceptanceStatus,OpportunityID,CRMPartnerAccountKey
Deal registered andapproved for scorecard.Oct-2018 cutoff appliesfor FX rates.Data: RegistrationDate,ApprovalDate, Status
Deal moves throughsales stages. Velocitymetrics computed.Data: PartnerSalesStage,ApprovalVelocity,CloseVelocity
Financial values convertedto USD. Won/Closed statusdetermined.Data: DealValueCD,PartnerRevenueCD,BilledRevenueStatus
Critical Business Rules Applied During the Lifecycle:

•  ClosedPartnerDeals = 1  when  PartnerSalesStage IN ('Support 100%', 'Deploy 100%', 'MS Win 100%', 'Disengaged 0%', 'Loss 0%')
•  PartnerDealsAcceptance = 1  when  OpportunityID linked + valid PartnerDealID + known CRM Partner + AcceptanceStatus = 'Accepted'
•  ISVDealsReporting = 1  when  OpportunityID linked + CRM partner's IsCoSellReadyPartnerAccount = 'true'
•  IsDealAccepted = 'Yes'  when  IsDealWithPartnerGTM = 1 AND (Microsoft or Partner sub-status = 'Accepted')
•  IsOpportunityWon = 'Yes'  when  IsDealWithPartnerGTM = 1 AND (BilledRevenueStatus = 'Won' OR ConsumptionStatus = 'Closed' + Reason = 'Completed')
How co-sell deals flow between Microsoft and Partners

The partner identifies a customer opportunity and refers it TO Microsoft through Partner Center.Business meaning: The partner is bringing Microsoft into their deal.Velocity metric: VelocityOfInboundDeals measures how many days it takes Microsoft to create an MSX Opportunity after receiving the partner's referral.Logic from code:  IF Direction = 'Inbound' AND OpportunityCreatedDate IS NOT NULL:    VelocityOfInboundDeals = DATEDIFF(OpportunityCreatedDate, CreatedDate)    (minimum 1 day if same-day)  ELSE: 0 (not applicable)

Microsoft identifies an opportunity and refers it TO a partner through Partner Center.Business meaning: Microsoft is inviting a partner to collaborate on their deal.Velocity metric: Not tracked via VelocityOfInboundDeals (= 0 for outbound). Instead, PartnerDealsAcceptance tracks whether the partner accepted the referral.Key flag:  PartnerDealsAcceptance = 1 when:    • OpportunityID exists (deal was linked)    • PartnerDealID is valid    • CRM Partner is known (PartnerName IS NOT NULL)    • PartnerAcceptanceStatus = 'Accepted'

Private deals (ReferralSubType = 'private - pc') have special geography handling: CustomerGeographyKey is forced to 0 and ReportingGeographyKey to -9999. The PartnerOneReportingKey falls back to the Bridge table with SubsidiaryID = -9999.
The Oct-2018 cutoff rule and multi-source exchange rate fallback strategy

All financial metrics are stored in USD. Because deals originate in local currencies from Partner Center and MSX, the system uses exchange rates from multiple sources with a date-dependent priority order.
THE OCT-2018 RULE:  RegistrationDate < 2018-10-01 → Opportunity rate preferred first  |  RegistrationDate >= 2018-10-01 → Partner Deal rate preferred first
DealValue / CurrencyExchangeRate (from Currency table by CurrencyID)
Pre-Oct 2018: Opportunity rate → Partner Deal rate → 1Post-Oct 2018: Partner Deal rate → Opportunity rate → 1
Pre-Oct 2018: Opportunity → Partner Deal → Currency table → 1Post-Oct 2018: Partner Deal → Currency table → Opportunity → 1

WHY THIS MATTERS:  The fallback chain ensures no deal has NULL financial values. If the preferred exchange rate source is missing (e.g., Opportunity has no currency code), the system gracefully falls back to the next source. The Oct-2018 cutoff reflects a historical change in how Partner Center recorded currency vs. how MSX did — older deals trust Opportunity rates more; newer deals trust Partner Deal rates.
How deals get categorized — the exact business logic behind each flag
PartnerDealID IS NOT NULL AND PartnerSalesStage IN('Support 100%', 'Deploy 100%', 'MS Win 100%', 'Disengaged 0%', 'Loss 0%')
Identifies deals that reached a terminal stage (positive or negative). Used for deal completion counts.
OpportunityID IS NOT NULL AND PartnerDealID IS NOT NULLAND CRM.PartnerName IS NOT NULL AND AcceptanceStatus = 'Accepted'
Measures partner engagement quality — did the partner formally accept AND link to an opportunity with a known CRM account?
OpportunityID IS NOT NULL AND CRM.IsCoSellReadyPartnerAccount = 'true'
Gates ISV deal counting. The partner's CRM account must be flagged as co-sell ready. This is a partner-level attribute, not a deal-level one.
Filters YTD counts to only approved deals in Enterprise (EPG) and SMB (SMS&P) segments.
GTM-filtered acceptance. Both sides (Microsoft and Partner) can trigger acceptance. This is the SAL (Sales Accepted Lead) gate.
Two paths to 'Won': traditional billing (Won) or consumption-based closure. Both require GTM program participation.
IF IsOpportunityWon='Yes' THEN 'Pipeline Wins-SAL-Partner Deals'ELIF IsDealAccepted='Yes' THEN 'SAL-Partner Deals'ELIF IsDealWithPartnerGTM=1 THEN 'Partner Deals'
Funnel categorization for pipeline reporting. Each deal falls into exactly one tier based on its furthest progression.
Measuring speed and effectiveness through the co-sell funnel
How many days from deal creation to approval. Zero if not yet approved. Directly measures the internal processing speed of the co-sell workflow. High values signal bottlenecks in deal review.
Total lifecycle duration from creation to close/due date. Measures end-to-end deal cycle time. Used alongside ApprovalVelocity to identify where time is spent (pre-approval vs. post-approval).
Same as ApprovalVelocity but in months for trend reporting. Used in monthly aggregation dashboards.

ONLY for Inbound deals. Measures Microsoft's response time — how quickly an MSX Opportunity was created after partner's referral. Minimum = 1 day (same-day response counts as 1, not 0). Zero for Outbound deals (not applicable).
Guard flags that filter out deals from average calculations. A deal without an ApprovalDate shouldn't pull down the average — these flags ensure only deals with valid dates are included.
1 = Deal with linked Opportunity (co-sell with visibility), 3 = Deal without Opportunity (referral only, no MS engagement yet). Drives the MSX Partner Sharing Categorization analysis.
TRANCHE LOGIC:  PartnerRevenueCD > $1M → 'High' tranche  |  ≤ $1M → 'Low' tranche  |  PRCD (capped revenue) = MIN(PartnerRevenueCD, $2M) — prevents outlier deals from skewing aggregates
The chain that maps a raw MPN ID to a reportable partner entity

Partners register with Microsoft using MPN IDs (Microsoft Partner Network). But a single partner organization may have multiple MPN IDs across subsidiaries. The CoSell pipeline resolves this into a unified hierarchy:
Raw ID from thepartner's referral

1. PRIMARY PATH:  MPNId_PartnerCenter → PartnerMaster.SourceID → PartnerOneID   If the partner's MPN ID is found in PartnerMaster, use that PartnerOneID directly.2. FALLBACK PATH:  CRMPartnerAccountKey → CRMPartnerAccount.PartnerNumber → PipelinePartnerMaster.SourceID → PartnerOneID   If MPN lookup fails, traverse through the CRM account's partner number.3. SUBSIDIARY MAPPING:  PartnerMaster.SubsidiaryName → VWDimGeography.SubsidiaryID → PartnerOneSubKey   OR CRM path: PipelinePartnerMaster → ReportingPartnerOne.PartnerOneSubID4. REPORTING ROLLUP:  Bridge_CascadedPartnerOne joins on (PartnerOneKey + SubsidiaryID) → PartnerOneReportingKey   This is the final reportable identity used in Power BI.
The 3rd-of-month boundary rule that determines when a deal gets fiscal credit
When a partner deal is approved, it must be credited to a specific fiscal month for scorecard purposes. The recognition month is NOT simply the month of the approval date — a boundary rule applies:

THE 3RD-OF-MONTH RULEIF  DAY(ApprovalDate) > 3   OR   MONTH(ApprovalDate) = MONTH(RegistrationDate)    THEN  ScorecardRecognitionMonth = FORMAT(ApprovalDate, 'MMMM, yyyy')           ← Current monthELSE    THEN  ScorecardRecognitionMonth = FORMAT(ApprovalDate - 1 month, 'MMMM, yyyy')  ← Prior month
Day(2) ≤ 3 BUT same month as registration

WHY THIS EXISTS: Prevents gaming of scorecard timing. Deals approved in the first 3 days of a month (that were registered in a prior month) are likely 'carried over' approvals and should credit the prior month. This aligns with Microsoft's fiscal period close procedures.
How customer and partner geography is determined with cascading fallbacks
Geography is not a single field — it's resolved through a cascade of sources with fallback logic:

1. PRIMARY: From TPAccount (HQ account mapping via opportunity)   Opportunity → TPAccountID → CustomerHQAccountsDim → GPSubsidiaryID → DimCustomerGeography2. FALLBACK A: Account Number geography (if TPAccountKey = 0)   MSXCRMAccountNumber → Hub_vw_Account → Country → DimSalesGeography → SubsidiaryID3. FALLBACK B: Partner-reported subsidiary (if no account number)   PartnerDeal.SubsidiaryID → DimCustomerGeography4. EXCEPTION: Private deals (ReferralSubType = 'private - pc')   → CustomerGeographyKey forced to 0 (unknown)

1. Resolved via PartnerOneSub mapping:   PartnerMaster.SubsidiaryName → VWDimGeography.SubsidiaryID   OR CRM path → PipelinePartnerMaster → ReportingPartnerOne.PartnerSubsidiaryID2. PartnerGeographyKey = SubsidiaryID from DimGeography_Base3. PartnerCustomerGeographyKey: Cross-reference of customer geography's   SubsidiaryID back through VWDimGeography. Used when partner and customer   geography need to be compared.4. ReportingGeographyKey: Derived from GPSubsidiaryID → DimReportingGeography.   This is the geography used for management reporting rollups.

Multi-level hierarchy: SubsidiaryID → Country → Region → Area.  Separate dimensions exist for Customer Geography, Partner Geography, Reporting Geography, and Capacity Geography to support different slicing needs.
IP CoSell, ISV Connect & Marketplace Deals
Partner IP attribution, bundled ACR, and marketplace ACV logic

IP CoSell tracks deals where a partner's IP solution (app, service) is part of the deal.• IsIPPartner: From DimIPPartner — flags if the partner has registered IP in the deal• IPCoSellPartnerOneKey: The PartnerOneKey of the IP-providing partner (may differ from the deal partner)• IPPartnerOneReportingKey: Reporting rollup for IP partner, resolved through FactSolution → DimSolution → PartnerMaster chain• IsPrioritizedPartner: From MapSolutionPracticeIndustryCountry — partner has prioritized solutionsSNAPSHOT OVERRIDE: If PartnerDealSolution_Snapshot has data for a deal, its PartnerOneReportingKeytakes precedence over the solution-based mapping (COALESCE logic).

Marketplace deal registration and bundled ACR have special revenue handling:• IsMarketplaceRegisteredDeal = 'Yes':  PartnerRevenueCD uses MarketPlaceACV from snapshot  (instead of standard PartnerRevenueCD calculation)• IsBundledandPartnerReportedACRDeal = 1 when:  Partner reported ACR AND IncentiveType contains 'bundled'  OR deal is marketplace co-sell• D365MonthlyRevenueCD:  PartnerRevenueCD / 12 (monthly spread)  ONLY when: D365 EOP/Pipeline deal + ContractStartDate exists  + NOT a marketplace registered deal• HasD365IncentiveType = 'Yes' when solution has D365 incentive  ('internal biz apps ip co-sell', 'msft internal biz apps standard/premium')

ISV Connect:  ISVConnectAppKey links deals to specific ISV Connect apps (DimISVConnectApp). SellerCoSellIncentiveKey tracks seller incentive programs attached to solutions. ResourceGUID uniquely identifies Azure resources within IP CoSell deals for ACR tracking. IsIPSameAsCoSell and IsChannelSameAsCoSell flags identify when the IP/channel partner is the same as the co-sell partner.
Investment bridge analytics, funnel categorization, and budget tracking
CoMarketing is a specialized sub-domain tracking joint marketing investments and their ROI across solution areas, industries, and geographies.
Tracks TPM budget programs for co-marketing investments and partner funding allocations. Links investment dollars to specific programs.
Forecast amounts for co-sell pipeline and revenue projections across time periods. Used for budget-vs-actual comparisons.
Categorizes deals into funnel stages for pipeline analysis and conversion tracking. Two levels of categorization for different reporting granularities.
Partner investment requests and approved amounts for co-marketing programs. Tracks the ask-vs-approved gap.
Four-dimensional bridge tables that slice co-marketing spend by: geographic area, industry vertical, solution area (Azure/M365/D365/Security), and solution play (granular solution-level).
Monthly point-in-time snapshots of the opportunity pipeline. Enables month-over-month trend analysis without losing historical state.

CoMarketing has its own fact tables (FactOpportunityCD, FactEngagementMilestoneCD, FactSolutionCD, FactPartnerDealCD) and dimension copies (DimCustomerCD, DimOpportunityCD, DimTime) that are optimized for investment analysis.
What transforms at each Medallion layer and why it matters

Raw ingestionMinimal transformationSchema preservationTables:• Cosell_Bronze_CRP_Solution• Cosell_Bronze_SellInCountryCatRP• PartnerMaster (raw)Purpose:Landing zone. Exact copyof source for auditability.

Cleansed & conformedBusiness keys resolvedIntermediate calcsKey tables:• PartnerDeal_Intermediate• DimOpportunity / _int• Currency / ExchangeRate• PartnerMaster (mapped)• PartnerImpactNumberPurpose:Single version of truthfor each source entity.

Curated dimensional model80+ tables (Dim + Fact)USD-converted financialsCore tables:• FactPartnerDeal (central fact)• DimPartnerDeal / DimPartnerOne• DimOpportunity / DimCustomer• All classification flags computed• All velocity metrics calculated• CoMarketing module tablesPurpose:Power BI-ready star schema.All business logic applied.

• GetNotebookStatus() — checks if notebook already ran (0=skip, -1=error, 2=conditional skip). Prevents duplicate processing.• GetWorkspaceIDLakehouseID(StreamName) — dynamically resolves workspace + lakehouse IDs per environment. Same code runs in DEV/UAT/PROD.• GetPublishSchema() — returns versioned schema path. Enables blue-green deployments.• writeTable() / getDataframe() — standardized I/O with environment-aware paths.• Z-Order optimization applied to reporting tables for query performance. CI/CD via CoSell_Build_1ES.yml.
The reporting scenarios this data powers
• How many deals did each partner close this fiscal year?
• What is the average approval velocity by partner segment?
• Which partners have the highest deal acceptance rate?
• What is the deal value distribution across High vs Low tranches?
• What is total deal value (USD) by solution area and geography?
• How does partner-reported revenue compare to Microsoft-verified ACR?
• What is the marketplace ACV contribution to partner revenue?
• How do CoMarketing investments correlate with deal pipeline?
• How fast is Microsoft responding to inbound referrals?
• What % of referrals convert to linked MSX opportunities?
• How many deals are stuck without opportunities (PartnerDealsWithoutOppty)?
• What is the scorecard recognition distribution by fiscal month?
• Which ISV co-sell-ready partners are driving the most deals?
• What is the Partner Impact Number (PIN) across product lines?
• Are prioritized solution partners outperforming non-prioritized ones?
• How does the D365 incentive program affect deal closure rates?
CoSell is Microsoft's partner co-selling analytics backbone — it answers 'did the partner deal work, and how fast?'
Currency conversion uses a date-dependent fallback strategy (Oct 2018 cutoff) with up to 3 exchange rate sources per metric
Deal classification has 7 distinct flags, each with specific business rules — they are NOT interchangeable
Partner identity resolves through a 6-step chain from raw MPN ID to reportable PartnerOneReportingKey
The 3rd-of-month scorecard rule prevents fiscal gaming and aligns with Microsoft's period-close procedures
Geography cascades through 3 fallback sources with special handling for private (PC) deals
IP CoSell and Marketplace deals have separate revenue attribution logic (snapshot overrides, ACV substitution, D365 monthly spread)
The pipeline is fully environment-portable — same code runs in DEV/UAT/PROD via dynamic workspace resolution

texts:

CRM Cosell Deep dive.pptx.notes:
Let’s focus on GPSMart for this slide. 
The GPS Mart is the SQL Endpoint for users to pull data for their adhoc reporting asks and analysis

The connection details is written over here: Server: gpsmart.database.windows.net, ADW: GPSMart

For all the ACR Related data, you will find the views in azure schema in GPS Mart

I have mentioned the views which are mostly used  from azure schema in GPS Mart, and they are as follows: 
vw_Bridge_AzureConsumptionPartner- This view has the data for ACR partner association. The table which lies under this view Map_Association_Partner_PPR_OCPMart.
So the table which projects use from ADLS for Map Association Partner and the table which is used in GPS Mart is different.
The table Map_Association_Partner_PPR_OCPMart has limited columns and some filters which are needed only from PPR Perspective.

2. vw_Fact_AzureConsumption
This view has the revenue/consumption data along with the keys which are additive for ACR.

The views below these are dimension views which are self explanatory, but we will still go through them
The first view in dimension is the vw_Dim_AZPricingLevel which has the information for the pricing levels specific to Azure sales, and that is why it is known as AZ Pricing level.
The next is vw_Dim_AzureFRAGroup which has the data for Azure FRA Group, and we discussed what Azure FRA group means in the previous slides
The next in the list are Azure Offer, Azure Pricing Level, Azure Service Level, Azure Subscription, and Azure Service Influencer which we have discussed in detail in the previous slide.
And the primary keys for these tables are mentioned in the  column beside the view name and the table name

CRM Cosell Deep dive.pptx.title: GPS Mart views ER Diagram
CRM Cosell Deep dive.pptx.notes:
Now, once you know what table hold what information, it becomes easy to analyze and see how these tables must be related

This is a standard Star Schema where we the fact table is surrounded and related with the dimension tables around it except the bridge table which is further related for partner related data

All the keys which are there in fact table will have a related dimension and those will be the columns which will be used to take joins while creating the tables

For example, as you can see I want to see the data with AZ pricing level what I will do is that  I have AZ pricing level 2 key and I have the same key in the fact view and what I will do now is that I will join the view based on this key to view the consumption based on AZ pricing level 2 key. 
The next you can see is vw_Dim_AzureFRAGroup And to see the data for Azure FRA group 2 what will have to do is join the view of dimension and the view of fact based on Azure FRA Group Key and the exactly of the column is Dim_AzureFRAGroupID. 
The same thing is needed for all the dimension views which are related directly with the fact view


Then you can see that we have vw_Bridge_AzureConsumptionPartner which is a bridge view to join with the views which are related to dimensions of partner and partner association which are vw_Dim_PartnerAttachType and vw_ReportingPartnerOne. In order to see the data at partner level, we need to join the fact table with the bridge table and the bridge table with either the DimPartnerAttachType or ReportingPartnerOne based on what you are looking at. 


One thing which you must understand is what attributes in a query is additive and what attributes are not additive,
And this is not something which you should memorize, whatever attributes are related directly to the fact table are always additive, and whatever attributes need a bridge table are never additive. That is the reason of adding the bridge tables in the data model

CRM Cosell Deep dive.pptx.title: Important Queries
texts:
-- Marketplace Billed Sales Co-sell
WITH CTE_MBS AS (
SELECT DocumentID,
    ProductID,
    ServicePeriodDuration,
    PartnerOneReportingID,
    TPAccountID,
    MAX(TotalPriceCDAmountAnnualizedwithCap) AS MBSCosell 
FROM crm.vw_Fact_MarketplaceBilledSales
GROUP BY
    DocumentID,
    ProductID,
    ServicePeriodDuration,
    PartnerOneReportingID,
    TPAccountID
)
SELECT SUM(MBSCosell) FROM CTE_MBS

-- Total MBS

WITH CTE AS(
SELECT DISTINCT InvoiceKey,TotalPriceCDAmount
FROM crm.vw_Fact_MarketplaceBilledSales
)
SELECT SUM(TotalPriceCDAmount) AS TotalMBS FROM CTE

CRM Cosell Deep dive.pptx.title: Important Queries
texts:
--PRACR
WITH CTE AS(
SELECT DISTINCT FPD.PartnerDealKey
       ,FPD.ResourceGUID
       ,FPD.ApprovalAndReportedDate
       ,FPD.TrueACRConsumption
       ,DPD.PSXDealID
FROM [crm].[vw_Fact_PartnerDeal] FPD
INNER JOIN [crm].[vw_Dim_PartnerDeal] DPD ON DPD.PartnerDealKey = FPD.PartnerDealKey
WHERE [IsPartnerReportedACR] = 'Yes' AND FPD.[ApprovalAndReportedFiscalYear] = 'FY24'
)
SELECT SUM(TrueACRConsumption) AS PRACR FROM CTE

--DRACR

WITH CTE AS(
SELECT DISTINCT FPD.PartnerDealKey
       ,FPD.[AzureIPCosellDealReg]
FROM [crm].[vw_Fact_PartnerDeal] FPD
INNER JOIN [crm].[vw_Dim_PartnerDeal] DPD 
ON DPD.PartnerDealKey = FPD.PartnerDealKey
WHERE DPD.[IsAzurePartnerCosellDealEOP] = 'Yes'
)
SELECT SUM([AzureIPCosellDealReg]) AS DRACR FROM CTE

tables:
One Line Definition

$ Deal Registration ACR 

Limited co-sell program retires ACR comp bucket as artificial revenue credit & with related quota to all eligible sellers (Mechanics similar to FY23)

Detailed Definition
Artificial Revenue Credit (ARC) as calculated from Annual Contract Value (ACV) from won Enterprise & SMC-Corporate segment deals incorporating an Azure incentive eligible repeatable IP solution, registered by a partner using Partner Center. 
Must have a minimum deal size of $25,000 (USD) of contract value within the first year of the deal. ACV will automatically be calculated for multi-year contracts.
Approved ARC will be determined by the Sales Operations team through deal validation and reviews following established program rules. The ACV is determined and 30% of that value or $15k (whichever is higher, capped at $300K) is the approved ARC for bundled deals and 5% of ACV (capped at $50K) for BYOL deals.

Business Objective & Alignment to Solution Area Priority 
Business objectives is to preserve and safeguard revenue by providing our highest ACV value Top Tier partners a 6-month transition period wherein sellers will continue to receive ACR retirement for co-selling outside of MP.

End-customer must be Enterprise segment or SMC – Corporate.  In scope deals are those where the co-sell is occurring outside of Marketplace.

Solutions must be listed on Marketplace (they do not have to be transactable) and have the “IPCS Incentivized” designation, which shows that the solution has been technically reviewed and drives material Azure consumption across partner and customer tenants.

Total Contract Value excludes MSFT first party licenses, non- related services or any hardware. Renewal of subscriptions/licenses are also excluded.
